/*
 * The base reset. Vendored from Tailwind's preflight on 2026-08-27, when
 * Tailwind was removed from the build.
 *
 * ## WHY THIS FILE EXISTS, and why it is not "the bit we could not be bothered
 * ## to delete"
 *
 * The audit that motivated the removal read: "Tailwind contributes 8 KB of the
 * 45 KB public stylesheet for one class". The 8 KB is right and the conclusion
 * was half wrong, which a measurement settled rather than an argument. Of the
 * 8,356 bytes it emitted, 3,048 were the utilities layer, of which the served
 * HTML used exactly one rule (`.sr-only`), and roughly 1,150 were a
 * custom-property registration polyfill for utilities this site never asked
 * for. Both are gone. The remaining bytes are THIS, and this site has no reset
 * of its own and never has: removing it outright moved 5,700 computed values
 * across nine pages, including every element on the site losing its font.
 *
 * So the choice was never "keep 8 KB or delete it". It was "keep a reset you
 * cannot read because it is generated, or keep one you can". This is the same
 * reset, in a file, with the parts that existed only to serve Tailwind's own
 * utility generation resolved away.
 *
 * ## WHAT CHANGED FROM THE ORIGINAL, exhaustively
 *
 * 1. `--theme(--default-font-family, ...)` and `--theme(--default-mono-font-family,
 *    ...)` become `var(--font-sans)` and `var(--font-mono)`, which are the
 *    site's own tokens and were what those calls resolved to anyway.
 * 2. The `font-feature-settings` and `font-variation-settings` lines that
 *    accompanied them are dropped: every one resolved to `normal`, which is the
 *    initial value, so each was a declaration that did nothing.
 * 3. The `@layer base` wrapper is gone. There are no layers here now, and a
 *    layer with nothing to lose to would only change specificity.
 *
 * Nothing else is edited. A reset is a list of browser bugs and inherited
 * defaults somebody else has already been bitten by, and editing one to taste
 * is how you get bitten by them again.
 *
 * ## ORDER
 *
 * Imported at the TOP of app.css, which is where `@import "tailwindcss"` sat,
 * so everything in the site's own stylesheets still outranks it by source
 * position exactly as before.
 */

/*
  Set the default placeholder color to a semi-transparent version of the
  current text color in browsers that do not crash when using color-mix()
  with currentcolor.
*/

/*
  Make elements with the HTML hidden attribute stay hidden by default.
*
* LOAD-BEARING ON THIS SITE, not a formality. The search shortcut hint ships
* with the `hidden` attribute and is unhidden only when the listener exists,
* and it carries `.sr-only`, which sets its own `position`, `width` and
* `clip-path`. The browser's own `[hidden] { display: none }` is an ordinary
* declaration that a class rule beats; this one does not lose, so a hint that
* is still hidden is hidden from the accessibility tree too rather than merely
* being off screen.
*/

/*
 * THE ONE UTILITY THE SITE USED, written out.
 *
 * `.sr-only` was the single rule the served HTML took from Tailwind's 44-rule
 * utilities layer. Copied from that output rather than rewritten, so the
 * computed values do not move, WITH ONE EDIT: `border-width: 0` is `border: 0`.
 *
 * The edit exists because Tailwind's `.sr-only` was never the rule that won.
 * `post.css` declared its own copy, later in the cascade and on every page,
 * spelled `border: 0`, and that is what every `.sr-only` on the site actually
 * computed. `border-width: 0` alone leaves `border-style: solid` standing from
 * the `*` rule at the top of this file, on a border with no width, which
 * renders identically and reads differently. MEASURED: it was the only
 * computed-style difference on the whole site after the split, on three
 * elements per page. Matching what shipped is worth more here than matching
 * what was generated.
 */

/*
 * INTER, SELF-HOSTED SINCE 2026-08-21. Previously three requests to two Google
 * origins; now two files from this one.
 *
 * ## WHY, on a site whose whole argument is that Cloudflare can do everything
 *
 * The old shape was `preconnect` to fonts.googleapis.com, `preconnect` to
 * fonts.gstatic.com, and a render-blocking stylesheet from the first that names
 * files on the second. That is a SERIALISED two-hop dependency across two
 * external origins, each with its own DNS and TLS, before a single glyph can be
 * requested. It also let Google observe every visitor, and it forced
 * `style-src` and `font-src` to carry third-party origins in an ENFORCED CSP.
 * All three are gone: both directives are now `'self'`.
 *
 * ## WHAT THESE FILES ARE, and the claim they replaced was FALSE
 *
 * The recorded plan was to self-host from `assets/fonts/`, described as unused.
 * MEASURED 2026-08-21, and both halves are wrong. Those two files are NOT
 * unused: `build-og.mjs` and `check-logo.mjs` load them because Satori needs
 * TTF buffers to draw the social cards. And they are the wrong FACES: two static
 * weights, 400 and 700, against a stylesheet that asks for 400, 500, 600, 650
 * and 700 plus one italic. 51 of 63 weight declarations are 500 or 600, so
 * self-hosting from them would have silently synthesised the site's dominant
 * weights.
 *
 * These are the VARIABLE latin subsets, weight axis 100 to 900, so one file
 * covers every weight the stylesheet asks for and the 650 interpolates rather
 * than rounding. Byte-identical to what fonts.gstatic.com was already serving
 * to every visitor, taken from that endpoint, so this changes WHO serves them
 * and not WHAT is served. Inter is SIL OFL 1.1; see public/fonts/OFL.txt.
 *
 * ## THEY GO THROUGH THE BUILD, NOT public/, AND THAT IS THE CACHE FIX
 *
 * These `url()`s are PROJECT-RELATIVE, so Vite treats the files as assets,
 * emits them to `/assets/` with a content hash in the filename, and rewrites
 * these references to match. That matters for one reason: `public/_headers`
 * grants `max-age=31536000, immutable` to `/assets/*` ALONE, and its own
 * comment says why, that everything under it carries a content hash so the URL
 * changes whenever the bytes do.
 *
 * SHIPPED AT public/fonts/ FIRST, 2026-08-21, and that was the defect: a stable
 * path gets Workers Assets' default `max-age=0, must-revalidate`. MEASURED on
 * production: an ETag and a 304, so no bytes moved, but one conditional round
 * trip per navigation where Google had served the same files immutable for a
 * year. Self-hosting had traded a third-party origin for a revalidation.
 *
 * Fixed by making the URL hash-bearing rather than by widening the header rule.
 * A `/fonts/*` immutable rule would have been the tempting one-liner and it
 * would have been WRONG: these filenames were stable, so replacing a font would
 * have left a year of browsers holding the old one, which is the exact failure
 * `_headers` already records for the favicon. `_headers` is UNCHANGED by this.
 *
 * `unicode-range` is carried over verbatim. Without it the browser downloads
 * both files eagerly; with it the italic is fetched only when italic latin text
 * is actually rendered.
 *
 * `font-display: swap` matches what the Google URL asked for, so first paint
 * behaves as it did. The FLASH is shorter now only because the bytes arrive on
 * an already-warm same-origin connection.
 */

/*
 * font-display: optional ON THE NORMAL FACE, since 2026-08-28, and it is the
 * fix for a measured layout shift rather than a preference.
 *
 * MEASURED on /blog at 390x844 on Slow 4G with a cold cache: CLS 0.0674, one
 * shift, the tag-chip row re-wrapping and moving everything below it by a line.
 * Single-variable experiment: with the woff2 requests BLOCKED and nothing else
 * changed, CLS is 0.0000. The swap is the cause.
 *
 * swap promises the fallback immediately and the real face whenever it lands,
 * which means it promises a reflow at an arbitrary time. The size-adjusted
 * fallback below makes that reflow small, and small is not zero: measured
 * across weights 400 to 700, Inter is between 0.955 and 1.029 of the adjusted
 * fallback for the same string, so ONE size-adjust cannot match every weight
 * the site uses and a wrapping row will always be able to re-wrap.
 *
 * optional gives the browser a short block period and then commits: either
 * the face is there and it is used for the whole page load, or it is not and
 * the fallback is, with NO later swap. There is no arbitrary reflow because
 * there is no later swap to cause one.
 *
 * ## WHAT IT COSTS, stated rather than left to be discovered
 *
 * A reader on a slow enough connection reads that page load in the fallback.
 * That is Arial at Inter's metrics, which is the whole point of the face
 * below, so it is the right shape and the wrong typeface rather than a broken
 * page. The font is cached afterwards, so it is one page load, and the preload
 * in root.tsx puts the request in the first bytes of the document specifically
 * to win this race.
 *
 * ## THE ITALIC KEEPS swap, DELIBERATELY
 *
 * It is not preloaded, on purpose: it is 79,716 bytes needed only by a page
 * that renders italic latin text. optional on a face that starts downloading
 * late would mean it is essentially never used, which is not a tradeoff, it is
 * a deletion. Italic text is also a small fraction of any page, so its swap
 * cannot re-wrap a whole row.
 */

/*
 * THE ITALIC IS KEPT AS IT IS, AND THE COST IS 79,716 BYTES. Ruled 2026-08-26.
 *
 * It is the LARGER of the two faces, larger than the normal face this site
 * renders almost everything in. The options were to subset it further or to
 * keep it and say what it costs; the second was taken.
 *
 * What makes that affordable is the `unicode-range` below, which was already
 * here: a browser fetches this file only when it actually has italic latin text
 * to render, so a page with no emphasis never pays a byte. That is why it is
 * also NOT preloaded, unlike the normal face. Preloading it would download
 * eighty kilobytes on every route to serve the few that need it, and an unused
 * preload is worse than none.
 *
 * Subsetting was refused on effort rather than on principle. It needs a font
 * pipeline in the build, a new dependency, and a gate to keep the subset in
 * step with the corpus, and it saves bytes only on the pages that already
 * decided to pay them. If the corpus ever leans on italics the trade changes;
 * this is the note that says so.
 */

/*
 * THE METRIC-ADJUSTED FALLBACK, so the swap does not move the page.
 *
 * `font-display: swap` above renders the fallback immediately and replaces it
 * when Inter arrives. That is the right trade for readability and it has a
 * cost: the two faces occupy different space, so every line reflows at the
 * swap. MEASURED on the throttled profile the audits used, cold: CLS 0.0065 on
 * the home page, 0.0128 on a post, and 0.0737 on /blog where the shift lands in
 * a list of cards.
 *
 * ## INTER IS A VARIABLE FONT WITH AN OPTICAL SIZE AXIS, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE
 * ## REASON THE FIRST SET OF NUMBERS HERE WAS WRONG
 *
 * `font-optical-sizing` computes to `auto` on this site's prose, so Inter's
 * `opsz` axis moves with the font size: the small-text variant is wider and
 * more open, the display variant is narrower. Its advance width per em is
 * therefore NOT a constant, which is the assumption every metric-override
 * recipe makes. Arial has no such axis and measures the same at every size.
 *
 * MEASURED in a real browser against the real deployed font, 2026-08-26, over a
 * sample weighted like body text:
 *
 *   size    Inter/em   Arial/em   size-adjust
 *     16     82.3313    78.8799     104.38%
 *     17     81.9303    78.8799     103.87%
 *     20     80.7406    78.8799     102.36%
 *     32     75.9556    78.8799      96.29%
 *
 * A first pass took the ratio at 1000px, got 96.29%, and adjusted the fallback
 * in the WRONG DIRECTION for body text: measured after applying it, the
 * fallback ran 9.2% narrow against Inter where plain Arial was only 5.7% off.
 * The harness that caught it is the one that measures a `white-space: nowrap`
 * span, and the harness that missed it counted wrapped LINES, which quantises
 * to whole lines and reported a matching control.
 *
 * **So this face is tuned to 17px, the site's prose size**, and it is a
 * compromise at every other size by construction: one face carries one set of
 * overrides, and body text is what there is most of and what reflows most
 * visibly. Headings are tuned less well and are a handful of lines each.
 *
 * The ascent and descent come from the font rather than from the glyphs and do
 * not move with `opsz`; they are taken at 1000px, where `fontBoundingBox` is
 * not quantised to whole pixels as it is at 16px. Inter measures 0.969 and
 * 0.241 of the em; each override is that divided by the size-adjust, because
 * the override is expressed against the ADJUSTED em.
 *
 * ## WHY ARIAL, AND WHY ONLY ARIAL
 *
 * `local("Helvetica")` and generic `sans-serif` both measured IDENTICALLY to
 * Arial on the measuring machine, which is Windows mapping them onto it. Arial
 * ships on macOS and on most Linux installs too. A face carries only ONE set of
 * overrides, so naming several `local()` sources would apply Arial's numbers to
 * whichever resolved: on macOS that would be Helvetica Neue, measured 8.5% away
 * from Arial, and the adjustment would be worse than none.
 *
 * If Arial is absent the face contributes nothing and the stack falls through
 * to the generic families exactly as before. That is the previous behaviour
 * rather than a new failure.
 */

/*
 * THE SERIF, which sets public headings at 32px and up and nothing else.
 *
 * One variable roman WOFF2, latin subset, byte-identical to what
 * fonts.gstatic.com serves for Source Serif 4 v14. Its axes, read out of the
 * binary rather than claimed: `wght` 200 to 900, `opsz` 8 to 60. The type
 * levels below name `opsz` 32 and 48, both well inside that range, and
 * `check:fonts` is what holds the declaration and the file to each other.
 *
 * ## THE FAMILY NAME IS NAMESPACED, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF IT
 *
 * The declaration says "Source Serif 4 Web"; the binary's own name table says
 * "Source Serif 4". A reader with the retail family installed would otherwise
 * have a copy of it in the resolution path for the same name, and the two are
 * not the same file: the retail release carries axes and glyphs this subset
 * does not, so a heading could set at metrics nothing here has measured. The
 * suffix removes the collision entirely rather than relying on the cascade
 * preferring an `@font-face` family over an installed one.
 *
 * `check:fonts` carries the mapping explicitly, so a swapped typeface still
 * fails: the namespaced name is not a licence to put any file behind it.
 *
 * ## swap, NOT optional, AND WHY THAT IS THE OPPOSITE CALL TO INTER
 *
 * Inter is `optional` because it is the dominant face, preloaded, and a reflow
 * of body text under the reader is the worst shift on the page. The serif is
 * the LATE face: it sets a handful of heading lines, it is not preloaded, and
 * `optional` on a face that starts downloading late means it is essentially
 * never used. `swap` is only safe here because the fallback block below makes
 * the swap move nothing, which is measured rather than assumed.
 */

/*
 * THE SERIF'S METRIC-ADJUSTED FALLBACK, and the number that matters here was
 * measured against the WRONG FACE twice before it was right.
 *
 * MEASURED 2026-09-13 in headless Chrome against the binary above, by the
 * method app.css already records for "Inter Fallback": a `white-space: nowrap`
 * span, advance width per em, at the settings the levels actually ship.
 *
 *   case                          SS4/em   fallback/em   size-adjust
 *   h2      32px wght 600 opsz 32  38.8379    39.0430        99.47%
 *   h1      32px wght 680 opsz 32  39.3838    39.0430       100.87%
 *   h1      40px wght 680 opsz 48  37.9875    39.0430        97.30%
 *   serif   48px wght 600 opsz 48  37.4238    39.0430        95.85%
 *   serif   48px wght 700 opsz 48  38.1396    39.0430        97.69%
 *   serif   32px wght 700 opsz 32  39.5107    39.0430       101.20%
 *   display 52px wght 700 opsz 48  38.1394    39.0430        97.69%
 *
 * **Tuned to the h2 row, 99.47%**, on the same reasoning that tunes Inter to
 * 17px: one face carries one set of overrides, and the 2rem heading is the one
 * that repeats down an archive page. The spread across every serif case is
 * 95.85% to 101.20%, so the worst-tuned level is about 3.6% out, against
 * Inter's equivalent spread of 96.29% to 104.38%.
 *
 * ## THE TRAP, RECORDED SO THE NEXT PERSON DOES NOT FALL IN IT
 *
 * `font-weight: 200 900` below tells the browser this face covers every weight,
 * so it uses Georgia REGULAR at 600 and 700 and never synthesises a bold. A
 * ratio measured against the Georgia FAMILY is therefore a ratio against a face
 * that will never render, because the family resolves a real Georgia Bold at
 * those weights and Bold is wider. Doing exactly that gave size-adjust 85.27%
 * and MEASURED CLS 0.0603, a heading going from four lines to six when the
 * webfont landed: the adjustment was applied in the wrong direction, which is
 * the same failure the Inter block above records at 96.29%.
 *
 * ## MEASURED, both arms, same harness
 *
 * 390x844 at dSF 3, Slow 4G, CPU throttled 4x, cold cache, the font response
 * held back 2500ms so the swap lands after first paint, a `layout-shift`
 * observer installed before any document script, six seconds of settle.
 * Headings at 32px and 48px, weights 600 and 700.
 *
 *   with this block          CLS 0.0000, no shift entries, every heading holds
 *                            its height and width across the swap
 *   without it (Georgia)     CLS 0.0016, the 48px/600 heading 276px -> 221px
 *
 * The control arm is what makes the zero mean anything: an instrument that
 * reports 0.0000 for both configurations has measured nothing.
 *
 * ## WHY GEORGIA, AND WHY ONLY GEORGIA
 *
 * Same rule as Arial above: a face carries ONE set of overrides, so naming
 * several `local()` sources would apply Georgia's numbers to whichever
 * resolved. Times New Roman was NOT measurable on the machine that took these
 * numbers (it did not resolve), so no second fallback face is declared and none
 * is guessed at. The stack still names Times and the generic `serif` after
 * this face; they simply carry no adjustment, which is the previous behaviour
 * rather than a new failure.
 */

/*
 * THE FONT STACKS. A plain `:root` block since 2026-08-27. Three since the
 * serif landed on 2026-09-13; it was two, and the heading said so.
 *
 * This was `@theme`, which is Tailwind v4 syntax and is how a token gets into
 * Tailwind's own utility generation. Nothing here ever needed that: no utility
 * on this site is generated from these, they are read with `var()` like every
 * other token in the file, and `check:contrast` parses the declarations
 * directly.
 *
 * WHAT MADE IT URGENT is that an unknown at-rule is DROPPED, silently and
 * whole. Removing Tailwind without this turned both stacks into nothing:
 * MEASURED on the build without it, every element on every page computed
 * `font-family: "Times New Roman"`, which is what a browser does when the
 * declaration it was given resolves to an empty custom property.
 */

/*
 * THE STACKING SCALE. One owner per layer, and the layers are NAMED.
 *
 * MEASURED 2026-08-28 before this existed: 24 `z-index` declarations across
 * eight stylesheets carrying 14 distinct values, three of which were 44, 45 and
 * 46. Values one apart are not a scale; they are the record of somebody adding
 * one to whatever was already there, and the next person has nowhere to put a
 * layer between them.
 *
 * ## THE REMAP IS PROVABLY INVISIBLE, which is why it could be done at once
 *
 * `z-index` is compared ORDINALLY inside a stacking context. Only the order of
 * two values decides which paints on top, never their difference. The mapping
 * below is strictly increasing on both sides, so every pairwise comparison in
 * the whole stylesheet gives the same answer it gave before, and no element
 * moved. Every old value was positive, so nothing crossed the implicit zero an
 * un-indexed positioned element sits at.
 *
 * The gaps are the point: there is room for a layer between any two of these
 * without touching the ones around it.
 *
 *   old  token              new
 *     1  --z-tile-raise      10   lifted inside a card, above its own siblings
 *     2  --z-tile-body       20   the card's body, above those
 *     3  --z-tile-action     30   an action that must clear the body
 *    15  --z-sticky         100   sticky inside a scrolling pane
 *    20  --z-dropdown       200   a menu or panel anchored to a control
 *    30  --z-popover        300   an editor popover, over the dropdown layer
 *    35  --z-drawer-scrim   400   the dim behind the mobile admin drawer
 *    40  --z-drawer         500   the drawer itself
 *    44  --z-pinned-bar     600   a pinned bulk-action bar
 *    45  --z-overlay-scrim  700   the dim behind a detail overlay
 *    46  --z-overlay        800   the overlay itself
 *    50  --z-progress       900   the reading progress bar
 *    60  --z-transient     1000   a toast, a modal layer, a footnote preview
 *   100  --z-skip-link     2000   always last, and it must beat everything
 *
 * NOT IN THE COLOUR BLOCKS, deliberately. `check:contrast` walks those and
 * requires a literal hex that participates in a measured pair; a stacking level
 * is neither. It sits with the font tokens, which are here for the same reason.
 */

/*
 * THE PUBLIC HEADER'S THREE LAYERS, on the scale above, decided 2026-09-13 and
 * written here so build 2 does not rediscover it.
 *
 *   the fixed bar      --z-pinned-bar   600
 *   the overlay menu   --z-overlay      800
 *   the skip link      --z-skip-link   2000
 *
 * **NOT --z-dropdown.** It is 200, which sits BELOW the bar, and the overlay
 * menu hangs past the bar's own block-size and must clear it. The name reads
 * like the right one and is the trap.
 *
 * Part A step 6b asked for these three renumbered to 10 / 20 / 30 under the
 * names --z-pinned-bar, --z-dropdown and --z-overlay-scrim. Those names are
 * already taken here, at 600 / 200 / 700, with consumers, so the repo wins and
 * nothing is renumbered: the handoff was reasoning about a scale this site does
 * not have. The ORDER it wanted is what matters, and the three above satisfy
 * it, with the skip link above an open menu and the menu above the bar.
 */

/* "Inter Fallback" sits between the real face and the generic families, so a
     reader waiting for the download gets Arial at Inter's metrics rather than
     Arial at Arial's. It is not a font anyone ever sees named; it is the same
     Arial, measured to occupy the same space. */

/* The serif sets public headings at 32px and up and NOTHING else: never a
     control, a chip, the logo, the header or an admin screen. "Source Serif 4
     Web Fallback" sits between the real face and Georgia for the same reason
     "Inter Fallback" does, and it is the thing that makes `font-display: swap`
     on this face move no line. */

/* THE ELEVATION SHADOW, one owner. It was written out twice, on the pinned
     bulk bar and on the footnote preview, in two files, and the two happened
     to agree. Not in the colour blocks for the reason the stacking scale is
     not: check:contrast requires a literal hex in a measured pair, and a box
     shadow is neither. */

/* The Paper, Glass, Light type levels ----------------------------------------
 *
 * Ruling 65, Part A step 2. EIGHT levels, no more, and EVERY LEVEL IS FIVE
 * PROPERTIES rather than one composite value.
 *
 * ## WHY FIVE PROPERTIES AND NOT A `font` SHORTHAND
 *
 * `font-variation-settings` CANNOT RIDE IN THE `font` SHORTHAND. A level
 * applied as `font: var(--t-h1)` would silently lose its optical size and its
 * variable weight, and it would still render: at the wrong `opsz`, with nothing
 * anywhere reporting it. That is the same silent-clamp class `check:fonts`
 * exists for, arriving by a different road.
 *
 * So there is no composite `--t-h1`. There is no deprecated one either, and no
 * dummy kept for the transition: while one exists somebody will use it, and the
 * failure is invisible. A consumer sets the five properties, or it is not using
 * the level.
 *
 * NOTHING WAS DELETED TO GET HERE. The repo has never carried a `--t-*` token
 * of either shape; checked before writing this, and the design handoff's
 * instruction to delete rather than deprecate had nothing to act on.
 *
 * ## THE WEIGHT IS DECLARED TWICE, DELIBERATELY
 *
 * `--t-*-weight` feeds `font-weight` and the `wght` inside `--t-*-vars` feeds
 * the axis. They are not redundant: `font-weight` is what the font-matching
 * algorithm selects a FACE with, and `wght` is what actually positions the
 * variable axis once a face is chosen. A level that set only the axis would
 * match the face at weight 400 and then be told to draw at 620, and a level
 * that set only `font-weight` would leave the axis to the browser's own
 * interpolation. Both are set, to the same number, at every level.
 *
 * ## THE OPTICAL SIZE IS ALWAYS EXPLICIT
 *
 * `font-optical-sizing` is left OFF at every consumer, so nothing interpolates
 * on resize; `opsz` moves at one breakpoint only, 48rem, and only for the two
 * serif levels. Inter carries `opsz` 14 to 32 and every Inter level below sits
 * inside it, the lowest exactly on the floor at 14. Source Serif 4 carries 8 to
 * 60 and its two levels name 32 and 48. `check:fonts` binds each level's
 * request to the family its own `--t-*-family` names, so an Inter level asking
 * for 48 is a named failure rather than a silent clamp.
 */

/* Field labels, buttons, chips.

     WEIGHT 600, NOT 560. Step 2's axis table set 560 and step 6b restated the
     level at 600 when it drew the kit; the later step wins, and the earlier
     value is recorded in the commit rather than left as a second reading. */

/* Bar destinations and footer links.

     NO LEADING TOKEN. The level was declared with one and nothing ever set a
     line-height from it. A level member with no reader is not a scale hole the
     way a missing spacing step is: a reader that needs nav leading adds the
     token back in the commit that reads it. */

/* Subheads inside posts, papers and admin. The last Inter level, and the
     highest `opsz` any Inter level asks for. */

/* Page and post titles. Lands on exactly 2rem at 375, so the serif never
     sets below its floor. */
/* The home name line, once per site. 2rem at 375, 3.25rem at 1280. */

/* TRACKING IS NOT ONE OF THE FIVE, and is declared apart so it cannot be
     mistaken for part of a level. Only three levels carry any, and a level
     with none has no token rather than a token holding zero: a `0` that every
     consumer must remember to apply is worse than nothing to apply. */

/* THE STRONG NAV WEIGHT, a number for `font-weight`. Step 2 had no strong
     level at all; step 6b added it. The active bar destination, the current
     filter chip and a figure caption's lead-in all read it.

     ONE FORM NOW, AND IT WAS TWO. The companion `font-variation-settings`
     string carried step 6b's `opsz` 15 against `--t-nav`'s 16, and nothing
     ever read it. It went onto the carried token map when the bar came out of
     shell.css, which is the only reason a token nothing reads survived at all;
     it is deleted here rather than carried for a build that would have to
     invent a use for it. The one-step difference it recorded is in the commit
     that removed it and nowhere else.

     Step 2's "selected chip 640" has NO token here. Step 6b draws the selected
